quests.sentence: She submitted her application on the last possible day, and forgot to include the required references.
quests.correctAnswer: She submitted her application on the last possible day and forgot to include the required references.
quests.hint: 'And' joins two verb phrases sharing the same subject - not two full independent clauses.
quests.explanation: A comma before 'and' is only needed when 'and' connects two independent clauses (each with its own subject). Here, both verbs ('submitted' and 'forgot') share the same subject 'She,' so the comma is incorrect.

quests.sentence: The new legislation will require all companies, that operate in the financial sector, to submit quarterly reports.
quests.correctAnswer: The new legislation will require all companies that operate in the financial sector to submit quarterly reports.
quests.hint: Does the 'that' clause define which companies, or describe all companies? If it defines, it's restrictive.
quests.explanation: 'That operate in the financial sector' is restrictive - it defines which companies must comply (only those in the financial sector). Restrictive clauses never take commas.

quests.sentence: The CEO announced two strategic priorities growing the company's international presence and improving operational efficiency
quests.correctAnswer: The CEO announced two strategic priorities: growing the company's international presence and improving operational efficiency.
quests.hint: 'Two strategic priorities' announces a list - introduce the two items with the right mark.
quests.explanation: A colon after 'two strategic priorities' introduces the specific items. Two items joined by 'and' do not need a serial comma before 'and.'

quests.sentence: Many factors e.g. rising inflation energy costs and supply chain disruptions contributed to the economic slowdown
quests.correctAnswer: Many factors (e.g., rising inflation, energy costs, and supply chain disruptions) contributed to the economic slowdown.
quests.hint: 'e.g.' belongs in parentheses with a comma after it; the examples form a serial list.
quests.explanation: The abbreviation 'e.g.' (exempli gratia, 'for example') is enclosed in parentheses and followed by a comma. The examples it introduces use serial commas.

quests.sentence: Only those participants i.e. those who completed all three data-collection sessions were included in the final analysis
quests.correctAnswer: Only those participants (i.e., those who completed all three data-collection sessions) were included in the final analysis.
quests.hint: 'i.e.' means 'that is' and specifies exactly which participants - it goes in parentheses with a comma after it.
quests.explanation: 'i.e.' (id est, 'that is') is enclosed in parentheses and followed by a comma. It introduces a precise restatement or clarification.

quests.sentence: The methodology used in this study cf Williams 2022 for a full description differs from that employed in earlier investigations
quests.correctAnswer: The methodology used in this study (cf. Williams, 2022, for a full description) differs from that employed in earlier investigations.
quests.hint: 'cf.' (confer, 'compare/see') is a parenthetical cross-reference - enclose it with the citation.
quests.explanation: 'cf.' directs readers to a related source and is enclosed in parentheses. A comma separates the author from the year, and a further comma follows the year before the descriptive phrase.

quests.sentence: The decision (taken without consulting the board) proved catastrophic for the company.
quests.correctAnswer: The decision-taken without consulting the board-proved catastrophic for the company.
quests.hint: Should this astonishing procedural failure feel incidental or dramatic?
quests.explanation: Parentheses make 'taken without consulting the board' feel like a minor aside. Em dashes emphasise it as a shocking and consequential fact - more appropriate given the word 'catastrophic.'

quests.sentence: The merger announced last Tuesday-surprised many industry analysts who had expected the two firms to remain independent.
quests.correctAnswer: The merger, announced last Tuesday, surprised many industry analysts who had expected the two firms to remain independent.
quests.hint: Is the announcement date dramatic or simply informative? Which mark fits best for a news report?
quests.explanation: 'Announced last Tuesday' is a routine temporal detail in news writing - commas are the standard neutral choice. An em dash would give it unwarranted drama. The sentence is declarative and the 'who' clause is restrictive (no extra commas).

quests.sentence: She was exhausted she had been working for eighteen hours straight
quests.correctAnswer: She was exhausted; she had been working for eighteen hours straight.
quests.hint: Two closely related independent clauses - which mark is most appropriate in formal prose?
quests.explanation: A semicolon is the preferred formal choice for two closely related independent clauses. An em dash ('she was exhausted-she had been working…') is also grammatically valid but carries a more dramatic, informal tone. The comma alone creates a comma splice.

quests.sentence: For the purposes of this Agreement the term Confidential Information means any information disclosed by one party to the other whether in writing orally or by any other means that is designated as confidential or that by its nature ought reasonably to be considered confidential
quests.correctAnswer: For the purposes of this Agreement, the term 'Confidential Information' means any information disclosed by one party to the other, whether in writing, orally, or by any other means, that is designated as confidential or that by its nature ought reasonably to be considered confidential.
quests.hint: Long introductory phrase; defined term in quotes; parenthetical 'whether…or' clause with serial list; two parallel 'that' clauses.
quests.explanation: The introductory phrase takes a comma. Defined terms in agreements take single quotation marks. 'Whether in writing, orally, or by any other means' is parenthetical and takes commas; its three items use serial commas. The two 'that' clauses are parallel (no comma before 'or that').

quests.sentence: The Parties acknowledge that the obligations under this clause which shall survive the termination of this Agreement for a period of five years from the date of termination are essential to the protection of each Party's legitimate business interests
quests.correctAnswer: The Parties acknowledge that the obligations under this clause, which shall survive the termination of this Agreement for a period of five years from the date of termination, are essential to the protection of each Party's legitimate business interests.
quests.hint: A non-restrictive 'which' clause inside the 'that' clause gives the survival period - commas enclose it.
quests.explanation: 'Which shall survive the termination…for a period of five years' is a non-restrictive clause giving the duration of the obligation. It takes commas on both sides within the 'that' clause.

quests.sentence: Either party may terminate this Agreement with immediate effect by written notice to the other if the other party commits a material breach of its obligations hereunder and in the case of a breach that is capable of remedy fails to remedy it within thirty days of receipt of written notice requiring it to do so
quests.correctAnswer: Either party may terminate this Agreement with immediate effect by written notice to the other if the other party commits a material breach of its obligations hereunder and, in the case of a breach that is capable of remedy, fails to remedy it within thirty days of receipt of written notice requiring it to do so.
quests.hint: 'And' joins two parallel conditions in the 'if' clause; 'in the case of a breach that is capable of remedy' is a parenthetical qualification.
quests.explanation: 'And' joins two parallel conditions within the 'if' clause (not two separate independent clauses). 'In the case of a breach that is capable of remedy' is a parenthetical qualifier modifying the second condition and takes commas.

quests.sentence: In his famous essay Experience Emerson writes the years teach much which the days never know
quests.correctAnswer: In his famous essay 'Experience,' Emerson writes, "the years teach much which the days never know."
quests.hint: The essay title takes single quotes (British style); 'writes' introduces the quotation with a comma.
quests.explanation: Essay titles are enclosed in single quotation marks in British style. A comma follows the verb 'writes' before the direct quotation. The quotation is in double quotation marks.

quests.sentence: Orwell's assertion that prose is architecture not interior decoration and that the baroque is over remains one of the most quoted pieces of writing advice in the English language
quests.correctAnswer: Orwell's assertion that 'prose is architecture, not interior decoration, and that the baroque is over' remains one of the most quoted pieces of writing advice in the English language.
quests.hint: The exact quoted phrase is integrated into the sentence - use single quotation marks around it.
quests.explanation: Orwell's exact words, integrated as the object of 'assertion that,' are enclosed in single quotation marks. Inside the quotation, 'not interior decoration' is a parenthetical correction taking commas.

quests.sentence: The narrator's observation that the afternoon light sic was falling in long gold bars across the kitchen floor has been cited as evidence of the novel's painterly prose style
quests.correctAnswer: The narrator's observation that 'the afternoon light [sic] was falling in long gold bars across the kitchen floor' has been cited as evidence of the novel's painterly prose style.
quests.hint: '[sic]' indicates an unusual or preserved feature in the original text - it goes in square brackets inside the quotation.
quests.explanation: '[sic]' (Latin: 'thus') indicates that the text is reproduced exactly as found, including any unusual feature. It is placed in square brackets immediately after the word it annotates, within the quotation marks.

quests.sentence: The conference will cover topics including artificial intelligence machine learning data privacy and the ethical implications of automated decision-making
quests.correctAnswer: The conference will cover topics including artificial intelligence, machine learning, data privacy, and the ethical implications of automated decision-making.
quests.hint: Four items in a list - serial commas between all of them.
quests.explanation: A serial list of four items uses commas between each item, including before the final 'and.' This is standard in formal British writing.

quests.sentence: The menu offered a choice of smoked salmon and cream cheese or avocado and tomato open sandwiches
quests.correctAnswer: The menu offered a choice of smoked salmon and cream cheese, or avocado and tomato, open sandwiches.
quests.hint: Two paired options are being contrasted - commas clarify which items are grouped together.
quests.explanation: Without commas, the reader cannot tell whether there are four separate ingredients or two paired options. Commas around 'or avocado and tomato' clarify that the choice is between two pairings.

quests.sentence: He is survived by his wife Erin his son Marcus and his daughter Clara who is herself a noted novelist his son-in-law David and three grandchildren
quests.correctAnswer: He is survived by his wife, Erin; his son, Marcus; his daughter, Clara, who is herself a noted novelist; his son-in-law, David; and three grandchildren.
quests.hint: Each family member is followed by their name (appositive); one has a 'who' clause - semicolons between each person.
quests.explanation: Each name is a brief appositive following a family role. The 'who' clause adds non-essential detail about Clara. Because each item has internal commas, semicolons separate the five items in the list.

quests.sentence: If the board had acted on the warning signs that were clearly visible in the quarterly reports which the finance director had raised concerns about the company would not have found itself in its current position
quests.correctAnswer: If the board had acted on the warning signs that were clearly visible in the quarterly reports, which the finance director had raised concerns about, the company would not have found itself in its current position.
quests.hint: Restrictive 'that' clause; then a non-restrictive 'which' clause at the end of the conditional; then the main clause.
quests.explanation: 'That were clearly visible in the quarterly reports' is restrictive (no commas). 'Which the finance director had raised concerns about' is non-restrictive (commas). The full conditional clause ends with a comma before the main clause.

quests.sentence: Should any party fail to comply with a direction given under this section which in the opinion of the authority constitutes a serious breach the authority may without further notice suspend the relevant licence with immediate effect
quests.correctAnswer: Should any party fail to comply with a direction given under this section, which in the opinion of the authority constitutes a serious breach, the authority may, without further notice, suspend the relevant licence with immediate effect.
quests.hint: Inverted conditional; 'which' clause inside it; 'without further notice' parenthetical in the main clause.
quests.explanation: The inverted conditional clause ends with a comma before the main clause. The 'which' clause inside the conditional is non-restrictive and takes commas. 'Without further notice' is a parenthetical qualifier in the main clause and takes commas.

quests.sentence: If the preliminary results which are expected in November are positive we will proceed to the full trial which if successful could lead to regulatory approval within two years
quests.correctAnswer: If the preliminary results, which are expected in November, are positive, we will proceed to the full trial, which, if successful, could lead to regulatory approval within two years.
quests.hint: Two 'which' clauses - one inside the 'if' clause, one in the main clause; 'if successful' is parenthetical inside the second 'which' clause.
quests.explanation: Both 'which' clauses are non-restrictive and take commas. Inside the second 'which' clause, 'if successful' is a parenthetical conditional and takes commas.

quests.sentence: The strategy rests on three pillars first attracting and retaining the most talented people in the industry second building partnerships with the organisations that are reshaping the sector and third embedding a culture of continuous innovation and improvement throughout every level of the business
quests.correctAnswer: The strategy rests on three pillars: first, attracting and retaining the most talented people in the industry; second, building partnerships with the organisations that are reshaping the sector; and third, embedding a culture of continuous innovation and improvement throughout every level of the business.
quests.hint: Colon before the list; 'first,' 'second,' 'third' take following commas; semicolons between the long items.
quests.explanation: A colon introduces the list. 'First,' 'second,' and 'third' as sentence adverbs take following commas. The three items are long parallel gerund phrases - semicolons separate them.

quests.sentence: The new curriculum aims to ensure that students are equipped with the skills they need for employment that they develop as independent critical thinkers capable of navigating an uncertain world and that they leave school with a genuine love of learning
quests.correctAnswer: The new curriculum aims to ensure that students are equipped with the skills they need for employment, that they develop as independent critical thinkers capable of navigating an uncertain world, and that they leave school with a genuine love of learning.
quests.hint: Three parallel 'that' clauses all depend on 'ensure' - serial commas between them.
quests.explanation: Three parallel 'that' clauses as objects of 'ensure' form a serial list. Serial commas separate them, and repeating 'that' before each maintains parallelism.

quests.sentence: The investigation found that the firm had failed to implement adequate safeguards that it had misled regulators about the nature and extent of its exposure and that senior management had been aware of these risks for at least two years before the collapse
quests.correctAnswer: The investigation found that the firm had failed to implement adequate safeguards, that it had misled regulators about the nature and extent of its exposure, and that senior management had been aware of these risks for at least two years before the collapse.
quests.hint: Three parallel 'that' clauses all depend on 'found' - serial commas between them.
quests.explanation: Three parallel 'that' clauses as objects of 'found' use serial commas. Each begins with 'that' to maintain parallelism.

quests.sentence: The companies lawyer who had years of experience in intellectual property law advised them that its not to late to file for protection in the European Union
quests.correctAnswer: The company's lawyer, who had years of experience in intellectual property law, advised them that it's not too late to file for protection in the European Union.
quests.hint: Four errors: a missing apostrophe, missing commas around the 'who' clause, a wrong contraction, and a spelling error.
quests.explanation: 'Company's' needs an apostrophe for singular possession. The 'who' clause is non-restrictive and takes commas. 'Its' should be 'it's' (it is). 'To' should be 'too' (meaning 'excessively' or 'also').

quests.sentence: The self employed business owners which had been trading for fifteen years were informed by their accountants that last years tax return contained several errors
quests.correctAnswer: The self-employed business owners, who had been trading for fifteen years, were informed by their accountants that last year's tax return contained several errors.
quests.hint: Four errors: a missing hyphen, the wrong relative pronoun, missing commas, and a missing apostrophe.
quests.explanation: 'Self-employed' is a compound adjective and requires a hyphen. 'Which' refers to people - 'who' is correct. The 'who' clause is non-restrictive and takes commas. 'Last year's' needs an apostrophe for singular possession.

quests.sentence: The well meaning policy makers having consulted widely among healthcare professionals which had extensive experience in rural settings developed a highly innovative evidence based approach to address the long standing issue of mental health provision
quests.correctAnswer: The well-meaning policy-makers, having consulted widely among healthcare professionals who had extensive experience in rural settings, developed a highly innovative, evidence-based approach to address the long-standing issue of mental health provision.
quests.hint: Five errors: two missing hyphens, wrong relative pronoun, missing commas around participial phrase, missing comma between coordinate adjectives, two more missing hyphens.
quests.explanation: 'Well-meaning' and 'policy-makers,' 'evidence-based,' and 'long-standing' all require hyphens as compound adjectives or nouns. 'Which' referring to professionals should be 'who.' The participial phrase 'having consulted widely…' takes commas. 'Highly innovative' and 'evidence-based' are coordinate adjectives and take a comma between them.

quests.sentence: The governments flagship housing policy which was unveiled with considerable fanfare eighteen months ago and which was described by the prime minister as a once in a generation opportunity to fix the broken housing market has according to an independent assessment failed to meet any of its three key targets
quests.correctAnswer: The government's flagship housing policy, which was unveiled with considerable fanfare eighteen months ago and which was described by the prime minister as a 'once-in-a-generation opportunity to fix the broken housing market,' has, according to an independent assessment, failed to meet any of its three key targets.
quests.hint: Possessive; 'which' clause with two parts; quoted coined phrase (hyphenated); parenthetical 'according to…'.
quests.explanation: 'Government's' needs an apostrophe. The non-restrictive 'which' clause with two parts takes one pair of commas. 'Once-in-a-generation' is a hyphenated compound adjective in the quoted phrase. 'According to an independent assessment' is parenthetical and takes commas.

quests.sentence: It is tempting to dismiss these findings as an outlier but to do so would be to ignore a growing body of evidence that taken together suggests the standard model which has underpinned our understanding of the field for three decades may need to be fundamentally revised
quests.correctAnswer: It is tempting to dismiss these findings as an outlier, but to do so would be to ignore a growing body of evidence that, taken together, suggests the standard model, which has underpinned our understanding of the field for three decades, may need to be fundamentally revised.
quests.hint: 'But' joining two clauses; 'taken together' parenthetical; non-restrictive 'which' clause.
quests.explanation: A comma before 'but' joining two independent clauses. 'Taken together' is a parenthetical adverb phrase and takes commas. The 'which' clause is non-restrictive and takes commas.

quests.sentence: What the data reveal and this is perhaps the most striking aspect of the entire study is not that the intervention failed for those who received it but that so few of those who were eligible to receive it actually did so a finding that points to profound systemic failures in delivery
quests.correctAnswer: What the data reveal-and this is perhaps the most striking aspect of the entire study-is not that the intervention failed for those who received it, but that so few of those who were eligible to receive it actually did so, a finding that points to profound systemic failures in delivery.
quests.hint: Em dashes for the emphatic aside; 'not…but' contrast with comma; closing appositive with comma.
quests.explanation: 'And this is perhaps the most striking aspect of the entire study' is an emphatic parenthetical and takes em dashes. 'Not…but' contrasting two 'that' clauses takes a comma before 'but.' The closing appositive 'a finding that points to…' takes a preceding comma.
